title: Queue collapse postmortem and action plan: probabilistic admission, prewarm & fairness
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: On 2026-02-27 a hosted API capacity event caused prolonged queue buildup and cascading throttling that produced widespread 429s and elevated latencies for several mid-tier customers. This ticket captures the postmortem findings and a prioritized action plan focused on: 1) avoiding synchronized queue collapse during churny multi-tenant spikes, 2) improving admission granularity to be token-cost aware, and 3) introducing lightweight prewarm and fairness controls to keep critical flows progressing. The goal is to reduce the probability of a repeat event and provide safe fallbacks that keep the API usable under stress.
root_cause: A confluence of factors: sudden multi-tenant arrival patterns with many long-streaming requests caused KV cache miss amplification; autoscaler hysteresis plus slow pod prewarm resulted in deficit in available inference workers; the admission controller used coarse request-count caps (not token-cost) which led to tenant starvation and synchronized shedding; and a lack of tenant-level queue telemetry prevented rapid diagnosis and targeted mitigation.
timeline_summary: 2026-02-27 03:10 UTC: start of unusual traffic spike from two customers running long-context batched jobs. 03:20-03:45: GPU pools hit saturation, queue depth increases, autoscaler begins scale-up but prewarm latency ~90s. 03:50: admission gate engages coarse throttles; many tenants observed 429s. 04:30: manual emergency evictions and capacity priming reduced backlog. 05:10: incident resolved to acceptable levels. Postmortem 03/01 convened and corrective engineering work scoped.
mitigations_completed: Emergency manual priming script used to pre-warm hot pools during incident
Temporary increase in per-region burst capacity allocation to relieve immediate pressure
Short-term admission tweak: increased per-tenant burst tokens for SLO customers
proposed_action_items: Implement probabilistic token-cost admission: estimate request token cost (input+expected output) and drop/admit probabilistically to avoid synchronized drops
Introduce tenant-weighted fairness queue: maintain small per-tenant reservoirs to prevent single tenant amplifying full-pool queues
Prewarm small reserve pool for rapidly-scaling models and introduce a predictive prewarm heuristic (ramp-rate detection)
Refactor admission controller to be token-aware rather than solely request-count-based
Add dynamic fallback routes: on admission pressure, automatically route long-sequence requests to quantized or lower-context variants when compatible
Improve telemetry: per-tenant queued-token gauges, per-model KV-cache miss rates, and autoscaler prewarm latency histograms
Update runbooks: clear decision tree for when to trigger manual priming, emergency capacity increase, and customer communication templates
Simulate tenant ramp scenarios in chaos tests and load-tests with long-tail sequence distributions

acceptance_criteria: Probabilistic admission deployed to canary region with no regressions against p95 latency
Per-tenant queued-token telemetry visible in Console and triggers alerts at configured thresholds
Chaos test that previously reproduced the collapse (long-tail multi-tenant spike) shows at least 10x reduction in severe 429 events in synthetic runs
Runbook contains clear steps and has been exercised in a tabletop drill
testing_plan: Create synthetic load test that mimics previous incident: 50 tenants with 5 high-seq tenants that ramp from 0 to 200 concurrent long-sequence requests in <10 minutes. Run tests in canary and staging with probabilistic admission toggled. Measure queued-token distribution, per-tenant fairness, and autoscaler prewarm latency. Add chaos test that kills 30% of warm nodes during ramp to validate graceful degradation paths.
monitoring_changes: Dashboard: per-region queue heatmap and top contributors
